newsitem.title: USA: Lawyers for King's assassin urge new gun tests.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers for King's assassin urge new gun tests.

text.p: Lawyers for the convicted killer of Martin Luther King Jr. told a court on Thursday that sophisticated new tests could prove the gun used to kill the civil rights leader in 1968 was never found.

James Earl Ray, who pleaded guilty to the slaying but later recanted, "has always alleged that the rifle in evidence is not the murder weapon but a throw-down gun," William Pepper, Ray's lawyer, told Shelby County Criminal Court Judge Joseph Brown.

Ray, whose confession spared him a trial and possible death sentence, was sentenced to 99 years in prison. But his lawyers now contend a trial would prove he was only a pawn in a conspiracy and confirm his innocence in the killing.

To open the door for such a trial, Pepper urged the court to allow the defence to submit the Remington hunting rifle to new electron microscope tests which, he said, would prove it did not fire the bullet that struck down King. A firearms testing expert testified that the bullet, now fragmented, was still "in good condition" for testing and "not deformed."

King's widow Coretta and son Dexter support Ray's request for a trial. With the two of them looking on in the crowded courtroom, Pepper said: "In the 28-year history of this case, (Ray) has never had the right to test this rifle. The defence has never had the right to have access to FBI test fire work sheet reports nor House Select Committee test fire work sheet reports.
"What we are seeking here for the first time ... is an oppportunity to test this rifle in an effort to exclude it for all time as the murder weapon."

Mrs. King later testified that a trial is "our last hope to reveal the truth about my husband's assassination." If Ray is denied a trial, she said, "our family and indeed the whole nation will be denied the due process of law."

Ray's fingerprints were on the rifle when it was found near a rooming house from which the shot that killed King was believed to have been fired. But both the FBI and the House investigative committee to which Pepper referred came up with inconclusive results when they tried to match the fatal bullet with the rifle.

The congressional panel concluded that Ray was the sole assassin. But Pepper has said that he believed King was shot by someone hiding in a bush outside the rooming house and that the slaying was a plot that involved the Mafia.
Other conspiracy theorists have blamed the FBI and even the U.S. military.
Ray, now 68 and dying of liver disease, is in a Nashville jail and did not attend the hearing. Pepper told the judge that "time is clearly of the essence" given Ray's grave condition.
King's death at the age of 39 came at an epochal time in the black civil rights struggle in the United States. It triggered urban rioting that wracked the country for days afterwards.

If Brown recommends the new ballistics test, a decision on a trial would hinge on what the tests produce. Ray has claimed he bought the rifle on orders from a mysterious man he could identify only as "Raoul" whom he had met in a Montreal bar.

After the assassination Ray, an inept petty criminal, fled to Atlanta, Toronto and then Europe. He was finally arrested two months after the killing at London's Heathrow Airport following a bank robbery that netted him little more than $200.
